chapter: The Paradise and life in Queens
title: Changing drummers at the Paradise: Timmie Kennedy to Kalil
summary: He replaced Tim Kennedy with Kalil for more experience against visiting stars, and sometimes used Art Blakey, Kenny Clarke or Max Roach.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Sadik and he worked with you...

At the Paradise, yeah, he stayed with me a long time. I saw Timmie the other night at the Village Vanguard and I...you see I had to change drummers because, you know, all these guys, Gene Ammons, and Bird, and all these guys would come up there and Art Blakey and Max Roach and all these guys, so I had to get a drummer with just a little bit more experience and it broke my heart and I know it hurt him too, you know, but he understood, you know. Yeah.

I got Kalil. And then sometimes I had Art Blakey, you know, if he wasn't doin' nothin'. And then Jo Jones, old man Jo Jones. Yeah. Because Kalil started gettin' popular and he started, you know, takin' jobs. I didn't blame him for that, you know, because bein' at the Paradise everybody heard him. That was the spot, you know, so I didn't say nothin'.
What was the sequence of drummers?

Timmie was there for a while, then Kalil, then he'd take off, I'd get Art Blakey, or I'd get Kenny Clark or I'd get Max Roach, you know, because they were in there all the time anyway. (laughter) So I had my pick, you know. Who ever wasn't workin', you know.
